title: When the Asset Burns
premise: Beatrix Dunmore — currently living as 'Mara Voss' — discovers her safe house listed online with interior photos, meaning someone inside the protection program sold her out. Following the thread, she learns the extraction network that trained her, 'the Chancery,' has been quietly auctioning its own assets to the very syndicate she once exposed. With a dawn flight as her only exit, Beatrix chooses instead to stay and burn the Chancery's records, recruit two fellow assets, and trade her testimony for justice outside any courtroom. She escapes on the flight not as a protected witness but as the woman who dismantled her handlers, carrying her real name back for the first time in seven years.
about_author: X. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former compliance investigator who spent a decade inside institutional archives before turning to fiction. They write from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the North Sea coast, where they claim the fog does half the plotting.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Scrolling property sites out of boredom, Beatrix finds her safe house for sale — with photos of her own kitchen, her books, her life. The agent's name is one she recognizes from a burned case file. Emotional beat: cold vertigo; the illusion of safety collapses in a single afternoon.

chapters.title: Four Names Deep
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. She inventories her identities and the rules that govern them, then breaks the first rule: she calls the Chancery's emergency line. A calm voice tells her to stay put; extraction is 'being arranged.' Emotional beat: dread sharpening into suspicion — the reassurance sounds rehearsed.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches the House
chapters.summary: POV: Elias Renner, a disgraced Chancery handler. Renner admits to himself he flagged the listing months ago and was ignored. He drives toward Beatrix's town, torn between duty and guilt. Emotional beat: weary conscience stirring after years of complicity.

chapters.title: Photos of the Inside
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. She traces the real-estate photos to a syndicate front company — the same one she exposed seven years ago. Whoever listed the house knew her habits from the inside. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve; she stops being prey.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix, with flashback. A memory of her training: the Chancery taught her that rules are armor, then showed her how easily armor is reissued. Present-day Beatrix decides the rules were always the trap. Emotional beat: grief for the person she was before the program.

chapters.title: The Chancery Calls Again
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. The extraction flight is confirmed: dawn, a grass strip outside town. But the voice on the line asks a question only her syndicate handler would know. Emotional beat: confirmation — the network itself has been sold.

chapters.title: Renner at the Door
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Beatrix and Renner. Renner arrives unannounced, off the books, and tells her the truth: the Chancery is liquidating assets to cover debts, selling dossiers to enemies. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance between the burned asset and the ashamed handler.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Life
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. She and Renner map the Chancery's local node: a records vault beneath a shipping office, holding dossiers on every asset — including hers, and including the syndicate's payment ledger. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Second Asset
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. She finds 'Daniel Okoye,' another hidden witness living two towns over, and convinces him the program sold them both. He resists, then shows her his own listing. Emotional beat: loneliness breaking; two ghosts agreeing to haunt together.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: POV: Renner. He pulls old favor strings and learns the syndicate's buyer arrives the night before the flight to collect the vault's contents. Emotional beat: Renner choosing a side, knowing it ends his career and maybe his life.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Beatrix retrieves a buried identity — her real name, Beatrix Dunmore, kept in a safety deposit box she swore never to open. Emotional beat: quiet, aching reclamation; she reads her own name aloud for the first time in seven years.

chapters.title: Counter-Surveillance
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix and Okoye. The pair case the shipping office, discovering the syndicate has watchers on the vault already. A near-miss in a stairwell nearly exposes them. Emotional beat: taut fear; the hunt has reversed, and they are the ones hunting.

chapters.title: Renner's Confession
chapters.summary: POV: Renner. Over a bottle in a dead man's apartment, Renner tells Beatrix he trained her — and that he wrote the rule she's about to break. Emotional beat: forgiveness neither of them can quite grant, but both decide to use.

chapters.title: The Plan for Burning
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Three moves: copy the ledger, torch the vault, and send the evidence to a journalist and three prosecutors simultaneously so no one can bury it. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the plan is simple and almost certainly fatal.

chapters.title: The Buyer Arrives Early
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. The syndicate's collector shows up a night ahead of schedule, forcing the team to move tonight instead of at dawn. Emotional beat: panic compressed into purpose; the clock slams forward.

chapters.title: Vault
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Inside the records vault, Beatrix finds her original file — and learns the Chancery manufactured the crime she witnessed to recruit her. Emotional beat: the floor drops out; her whole exile was built on a lie.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Beatrix and Renner. The vault goes up. Renner stays to trigger the fire and cover their exit, telling her this is the only rule he ever kept. Emotional beat: sacrifice without sentiment; Renner's redemption priced in flame.

chapters.title: The Grass Strip at Dawn
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. The extraction plane waits, and the Chancery's surviving director offers Beatrix a new name, a new country, a clean erasure. Emotional beat: the final temptation — safety offered by the people who sold her.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Okoye, wounded in the vault escape, begs her to take the flight and leave the fight. She realizes the duty she owes is not to the program but to the people it consumed — and to the self she buried. Emotional beat: love, in its stubborn form, winning over fear.

chapters.title: The Director's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Beatrix turns the tables: she has already sent everything, and the director's own escape depends on the plane she now controls. She forces him onto the tarmac to face the arriving prosecutors. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, executed with terrifying calm.

chapters.title: Beatrix Dunmore
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. On the dawn flight — as a witness now, not an asset — Beatrix signs her statement with her real name while Okoye sleeps beside her and Renner's fire smolders on the news feed. Emotional beat: exhausted, unguarded peace.

chapters.title: After the Burning
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix, epilogue. Months later, testifying under her own name, Beatrix passes a house for sale with no photos of the inside — and smiles. She keeps the newspaper clipping of the Chancery's collapse in a drawer she never locks. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed; a life finally owned outright.
